name: Mintlify
look: Atmospheric sky-to-cream gradient bands, black pill CTAs, mint reserved for accents and confirmations.

hero.title: Documentation your developers actually read
hero.sub: Write in Markdown, get a fast searchable site with a generated API reference, and stop maintaining a docs framework nobody wanted to own.

features.title: Docs without a docs team
features.sub: The things every documentation site needs, without building any of them yourself.

items.title: Write in MDX
items.body: Markdown with components. Version it in the repo alongside the code it documents.

items.title: API reference generated
items.body: Point at an OpenAPI spec and get a reference with a working request playground.

items.title: Search that works
items.body: Instant full-text search with keyboard navigation, indexed on every deploy.

items.title: Preview per branch
items.body: Every pull request gets a live docs preview to review before merge.

items.title: Localisation
items.body: Multiple languages with fallback, so a partial translation is still useful.

items.title: See what people read
items.body: Which pages, which searches returned nothing, and where readers give up.

showcases.title: It lives with the code
showcases.body: Docs are MDX files in your repository. They review in the same pull request as the change they describe, which is the only mechanism that reliably keeps documentation current.
points: Reviewed in the same pull request

showcases.title: The failed-search report
showcases.body: The most useful analytics page is the list of searches that returned nothing. It is a queue of documentation your readers wanted and could not find, ordered by demand.

gallery.title: DOCUMENTATION
gallery.sub: Setup, components, API references and analytics.

testimonial.quote: The failed-search report is the only documentation roadmap we have ever actually followed. It is a list of things people wanted and could not find, in demand order.
testimonial.name: Ana Petrova

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Free for open source. Paid for private docs and analytics.

items.a: In your repository as MDX files. We build and host them; you keep the source and can walk away with it at any time.

items.q: How is the API reference generated?
items.a: From an OpenAPI or AsyncAPI spec, regenerated on every deploy, with an interactive playground that sends real requests.

items.q: Can I use my own domain?
items.a: Yes, on every paid plan, with the certificate issued and renewed automatically.
Full-text search indexed on each deploy, with a report of queries that returned nothing so you can see the gaps.

cta.title: Ship documentation today
cta.sub: Free for open source, and your Markdown stays in your repository.

notes: Atmospheric gradient bands — sky-blue into cream — provide the cinematic marketing presentation.
Mint green is reserved for accent CTAs, active states and confirmations. The primary button stays black.
One sans for all prose and a mono for code, inline code and type signatures.
The documentation layout is three columns — sidebar, prose, table of contents — with dense 14px body for long reading.
The radius scale is deliberately gapped: 12px for marketing surfaces and full pills for buttons, with nothing in between.
